## RULES established for `rustowl clean`

**CLI surface**
1. `clean` takes NO positional args and NO options except `-h/--help`. Any other token → clap error, exit 2: `error: unexpected argument '<tok>' found\n\nUsage: executable clean\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` (stdout empty).
2. `clean --help` / `clean -h` / `help clean` all print byte-identically to stdout, exit 0: `Remove artifacts from the target directory\n\nUsage: executable clean\n\nOptions:\n  -h, --help  Print help\n`. Usage line uses argv[0] basename.
3. Global flags before the subcommand are accepted and change nothing: `-q clean`, `-qq clean`, `--stdio clean` all behave exactly like `clean` (no LSP server starts).

**Algorithm (complete)**
4. Step 1: run `cargo metadata --format-version 1` — exactly those 3 argv items. No `--no-deps`, `--offline`, `--manifest-path`, `--filter-platform`.
5. Program = `$CARGO` if set (even if empty → spawn fails), else `cargo` via `PATH`. It does **NOT** use the sysroot cargo (`$HOME/.rustowl/sysroot/<tc>/bin/cargo`) even when it exists — `clean` bypasses `rustowl::toolchain` entirely.
6. Child cwd = the rustowl process's cwd. Child env = inherited, **unmodified** (no `RUSTC`, `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP`, `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`).
7. Child stdout AND stderr are captured and discarded — cargo's errors are never shown.
8. Non-zero child exit status → hard failure, JSON not examined.
9. JSON parsing = `cargo_metadata::MetadataCommand::exec()` semantics: split stdout into lines, take the **first line starting with `{`**, parse only that line. Proven by: garbage lines before a one-line JSON → works; pretty-printed multi-line JSON → fails; a decoy `{}` line before the real JSON → fails.
10. The payload must deserialize as a full `cargo_metadata::Metadata` (bare `{"target_directory":...}` is rejected).
11. Only the `target_directory` field is used. `build_directory` and `workspace_root` are ignored.
12. Step 2: `remove_dir_all(target_directory.join("owl"))`, and the `Result` is **discarded**.
13. Step 3: exit 0 unconditionally.

**Deletion semantics**
14. Exactly one path is deleted: `<target_directory>/owl`. Name match is byte-exact and case-sensitive — `Owl`, `OWL`, `.owl`, `owl2`, `owls`, `owl.d`, `"owl "`, `rustowl`, and nested `*/owl` all survive. No recursive search.
15. It is **not** `cargo clean`: only ONE cargo child process is ever spawned, and `target/debug`, `target/release`, `target/.cargo-lock`, `target/CACHEDIR.TAG`, `target/<anything-else>` survive.
16. Behavior matches `std::fs::remove_dir_all` exactly (verified against a compiled oracle): non-empty dir → removed recursively; empty dir → removed; **regular file → NOT removed**; symlink (to dir, to file, or dangling) → **the symlink is removed, its target is untouched**; missing → no-op; unwritable parent or unwritable `owl` → nothing removed (not even partially).
17. rustowl itself creates nothing. `Cargo.lock` and `target/.rustc_info.json` that appear are side effects of the real `cargo` child (cargo creates `.rustc_info.json` only if the target dir already exists, and creates `Cargo.lock` even when metadata fails at a later stage).
18. `$HOME/.rustowl` is never read or written: no sysroot check, no toolchain setup, no download. Works with `HOME` unset or nonexistent. `$HOME/.rustowl/owl` is NOT deleted. Runtime ≈ 0.07 s.
19. Zero log output. `RUST_LOG=trace|debug|info|warn` all yield byte-empty stdout+stderr.

**Target-dir resolution** (all inherited from `cargo metadata`, no rustowl-specific override)
20. Honoured: default `<pkg-root>/target`; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (absolute and relative); `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR`; `.cargo/config.toml` `[build] target-dir`. In each case only the *resolved* dir's `owl` is deleted and the default `target/owl` survives.
21. There is no `--target-dir` flag (exit 2).
22. Workspaces: only the single workspace `target_directory`'s `owl` is deleted — member `crate*/target/owl` survive, and running from inside a member still deletes the workspace-root one.
23. Running from a nested subdir of a package works (cargo walks up).
24. A relative `target_directory` in the JSON is used verbatim (resolved against process cwd); trailing slash and spaces/non-ASCII paths work.

**Silent-failure set** — all of these give exit 0, empty stdout, empty stderr, and delete nothing: no `Cargo.toml` anywhere up the tree (even with `target/owl` present), malformed `Cargo.toml`, `[workspace]` with no members, unresolvable dependency (no network), `cargo` absent from `PATH`, `CARGO` pointing at a nonexistent or empty program, cargo exiting 1 or 101 with valid JSON, unparseable/multi-line JSON, permission-denied removal.
25. No input was found that makes `clean` exit 1 or panic — only clap errors give a non-zero (2) exit.

Note: `/workspace` is not pristine — another agent created `/workspace/{Cargo.toml,Cargo.lock,src,target}` before my run there; I created nothing in `/workspace`. My authoritative "no manifest" cases are `/tmp/clean-9`, `/tmp/clean-9b`, `/tmp/clean-10`.

```
RULES ESTABLISHED — RustOwl v1.0.0-rc.1 logging/output

LINE FORMAT (all records -> STDERR, one write+flush per record)
  <ts> SP <level:{:<5}> SP '[' <target> ']' SP <message> LF
  ts   = "[year]-[month]-[day]T[hour]:[minute]:[second].[subsecond digits:3]Z"
         ALWAYS exactly 3 fraction digits, zero-padded (196/196 samples); literal 'T' and 'Z';
         ALWAYS UTC (TZ ignored; matches `date -u`); taken at record time.
  level word left-aligned padded to width 5 => "ERROR"/"DEBUG"/"TRACE" (1 space before '['),
         "WARN "/"INFO " (2 spaces before '[').
  Exactly one space after ts, one after level, "] " after target. Single \n, no \r,
  no trailing spaces, stream ends with \n.
  Message is verbatim: embedded \n makes a multi-line record with NO prefix on continuation
  lines; TAB/ESC pass through; invalid UTF-8 -> U+FFFD; no truncation (3088-byte line seen).

COLOURS
  Emitted iff stderr.is_terminal(). stdout's TTY-ness irrelevant.
  NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE / FORCE_COLOR / RUST_LOG_STYLE / TERM are ALL IGNORED
  (cannot disable on a pty, cannot force on a pipe).
  Only the padded level word is wrapped: ESC[<c>m + "{:<5}" + ESC[0m.
    ERROR=31  WARN=33  INFO=36  DEBUG=35  TRACE = no escapes at all (plain).
  Timestamp, target, message, banner and panic text are never coloured.

LEVEL FILTER
  default = Info  if a clap subcommand matched (check/clean/toolchain/completions)
  default = Warn  if no subcommand (LSP server; --stdio irrelevant)
  RUST_LOG overrides iff it parses as a single log::LevelFilter: off|error|warn|info|debug|trace,
  ANY case mixture, NOT trimmed. Everything else silently ignored -> mode default. This includes
  "", "1", "none", "warning", "err", " warn", "warn ", and all env_logger directive specs
  ("rustowl=trace", "trace,reqwest=off", "info,rustowl::toolchain=off").
  Single global max level; no per-module filtering; dependency crates share it.
  rustowl's own code emits NO debug!/trace! records (trace==debug==info for rustowl targets);
  DEBUG/TRACE only ever come from reqwest::connect / reqwest::retry.

-q / --quiet  (repeatable global flag; must precede the subcommand)
  NO effect on log level, banner, or anything else at 1..5 repetitions.
  ONLY effect anywhere: -V/--version prints "v1.0.0-rc.1\n" when quiet>=1 instead of
  "RustOwl v1.0.0-rc.1\n" when quiet==0.

BANNER (stderr, uncoloured, before any log record)
  b'RustOwl v1.0.0-rc.1\nThis is an LSP server. You can use --help flag to show help.\n'
  Printed iff NO subcommand matched (no args, --stdio, -q…, any mix). Suppressed by adding a
  subcommand (even `--stdio check …`). Not suppressed by -q…-qqqq or RUST_LOG=off.

STDOUT usage
  Only: -V/--version; -h/--help/help/help SUB/SUB --help/toolchain help; completions <SHELL>;
  and the LSP JSON-RPC stream. check/clean/toolchain* write NOTHING to stdout.
  clap usage/arg errors -> stderr, exit 2 (not log records). No log file, no window/logMessage.

PANIC BLOCK (std hook; not filtered by RUST_LOG or -q; never coloured)
  "\nthread '{name}' panicked at {file}:{line}:{col}:\n{msg}\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n"
  Note the LEADING \n (blank line). RUST_BACKTRACE=1 added no backtrace (stripped binary).

MESSAGE CATALOGUE (target -> level: message)
  rustowl -> ERROR "Analyze failed"
  rustowl::toolchain -> INFO: "sysroot not found; start setup toolchain" /
    "start installing Rust toolchain..." / "temp dir is made: {p}" / "start downloading {url}..." /
    "{:>3}% received" (RIGHT-aligned width 3: "  1% received".." 99%".."100%", one line per int
    percent 1..100) / "download finished" / "successfully unpacked" /
    "component {rustc|rust-std-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu|cargo} successfully installed" /
    "installing Rust toolchain finished" / "start installing RustOwl toolchain..." /
    "installing RustOwl toolchain finished" / "toolchain setup finished" / "remove sysroot: {p}" /
    "cargo is selected in sysroot/bin" / "rustowlc is selected in sysroot/bin"
    WARN: "cargo not found; fallback" / "rustowlc not found; fallback"  (sysroot/bin miss; PATH
    presence is irrelevant)
    ERROR: "failed to download tarball" / "{reqwest_err:?}" / "()" / "failed to create toolchain directory"
    The bare "()" line is emitted only by the implicit-setup caller (check/LSP), never by
    `toolchain install`. The RustOwl-toolchain step emits no "temp dir is made:" line.
  rustowl::lsp::backend -> INFO: "wait 100ms for rust-analyzer" / "stop running analysis processes"
    / "start analysis" / "analyze {n} packages..." (always plural; 0 and 1 observed)
  rustowl::lsp::analyze -> WARN "Invalid analysis target: {path as given}";
    INFO "start analyzing {abs}" / "stdout closed"
  reqwest::connect -> DEBUG "starting new connection: {origin}/"
  reqwest::retry   -> TRACE "shouldn't retry!"
  `clean` is COMPLETELY silent (both streams empty, exit 0) in every scenario, even RUST_LOG=trace.
  TMPDIR unwritable => "start installing Rust toolchain..." then exit 1 with no error record.

Overall: byte-compatible with `simple_logger` + with_utc_timestamps + SimpleLogger::env().
Gaps (detailed in the file): clean's default level unobservable; -q's intended purpose unknown;
n>=2 packages unreachable; second-panic `note:` behaviour untested; {err:?} payload text is
sandbox-network-dependent (this env has a flaky mock server for static.rust-lang.org/github.com).
```
